jd.title: Payroll Account Manager
jd.summary: Procare HR is hiring a Payroll Account Manager to own end-to-end payroll delivery for a multi-client book of business. This is a client-facing seat — you'll be the go-to person clients trust for accurate, on-time, compliant payroll across multiple entities.
jd.summary2: You'll process payroll for multiple clients with multiple EINs, resolve payroll issues with sound judgment, and build the kind of relationships that make clients stick around. Fully remote. $26–$30/hr, credit given for experience.
mustHave: 3+ years processing payroll for multiple clients (multi-state a plus).
2+ years with HRIS platforms (UKG Ready preferred).
Strong Microsoft Office skills, especially Excel.
niceToHave: Associate's degree in Accounting, Business, HR, or Finance.
Prior PEO / HR Shared Services experience.
Comfortable owning client relationships, not just processing.

lookFor.detail: Has actually run payroll across 8+ EINs, not just "supported a team that did." This is the rarest, most important filter.
Understands the operating model of serving many unrelated clients at once — different pay cycles, different rules, same week.
Title says "Account Manager" — they need to own the relationship, not just push numbers through a system quietly.
UKG Ready experience is a green flag, but any modern HRIS (ADP WFN, Paycom, Paylocity, iSolved) with real depth transfers fast.

questions.q: Walk me through how many clients and EINs you've processed payroll for at once — what did that workflow actually look like?
questions.internal: This is the hardest filter to fill. Vague answers ("I helped with a few clients") usually mean single-EIN, in-house experience dressed up. Push for specifics — how many EINs, how they tracked deadlines across them.

questions.q: Have you worked in a PEO or HR shared-services model? What was different about that versus in-house payroll?
questions.internal: PEO experience is "nice to have" on paper but it's actually a strong predictor of success here — the operating model is genuinely different from in-house payroll. Listen for real understanding, not just a resume line.

questions.q: Tell me about a time a client had a payroll issue or dispute. How did you handle it?
questions.internal: This role is titled "Account Manager" for a reason — the client wants someone who owns the relationship under pressure, not just someone who's technically correct and disappears when it gets uncomfortable.

questions.q: What HRIS platforms have you used, and how deep is your experience with UKG Ready specifically?
questions.internal: UKG Ready is preferred, not required — don't screen out a strong candidate on ADP/Paycom/Paylocity/iSolved experience. Listen for depth on any platform (built reports, ran multi-client processing) versus surface-level exposure.

matrices.boolean: ("Payroll Account Manager" OR "Payroll Specialist" OR "Payroll Coordinator" OR "Payroll Analyst") AND ("multi-client" OR "multi-state" OR PEO OR "shared services" OR "multiple EINs") AND ("UKG" OR "UKG Ready" OR "UltiPro" OR "ADP Workforce Now" OR Paycom OR Paylocity OR iSolved)

watchOuts.note: Strong in-house payroll admin with zero multi-client exposure will struggle with the volume and context-switching this role demands.
Technically sharp but avoids client conversations — wrong shape for a role titled "Account Manager."
Associate's degree is preferred, not required — don't auto-reject strong experience-only candidates.
